newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger as currency gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger as currency gains.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Thursday as further gains by the Canadian dollar and some technical factors helped boost prices in a quiet market, dealers said.

"The currency is holding in nicely. There's a technical situation in the threes and a technical situation in the one years. That's holding the curve in," said Walter Posiewko, a money market trader with Royal Bank Investment Management Inc.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.17 percent from 3.19 percent at the close of trading on Wednesday.

The Canadian dollar opened firmer on Thursday after supportive comments from Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen on Wednesday. Speaking in Halifax, Thiessen said it is important to maintain confidence in the dollar and that Canada could not maintain a completely made-in-Canada rate policy.

"The street is getting a little bit of comfort from the fact that the currency is holding in here and that there's a bid for this thing. But I don't think that this is an account driven market, this seems to be a highly technical market right now," said Posiewko.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.56 percent from 3.61 percent at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 4.12 percent, from 4.16 percent at Wednesday's close.

The call loan rate traded at 3.0-3.05 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range. Dealers said the rate was trading unusually low for a Thursday. On Wednesday, the Bank of Canada set reverses on the money market at 2.75 percent.
